bullets: Drainage is the single highest leverage design choice on any trail; ignoring it leads to rebuilding from scratch a year later.
The most common mistake new builders make is grading too aggressively; once internalized, the rest of the decisions get easier.
Land stewardship conversations have to happen before the first dig, especially on platforms like Spok and Wrench and Cascadia Alliance.
Bench cuts on hillsides aren't optional — the shortcut on day one becomes the washout on year three.
Soil structure matters more than people think, and it's a key factor in trail durability and erosion control.
Machine built versus hand built rails is a revised belief; the framing matters because it tells you which trade offs you're making.
The second order effect is the part most people miss when evaluating trail building failures.
A practical takeaway is to pick one of the covered ideas and run it for two weeks to test its impact.
